reason: The complete batch has repairable local defects. The signed-radius gap in the all-space gauge prerequisite can be supplied locally in its consumer. Two defects found in external suppliers are reported separately; the assigned arguments use unaffected clauses.

findings.reason: For arbitrary open Ω, u(Ω) need not equal R, so h determines F only on u(Ω), not globally. Also |ω| is called a frequency without its physical unit reading; with x⁰=ct in SI length coordinates, ω has units m⁻¹ and physical angular frequency is c|ω|. Qualify both claims.

Clause (c) uses sin and cos and asserts a rotation law, but the definition omits the trigonometric definition and addition-law suppliers. Add the exact mathematical prerequisites or leave the law to the proving lemma.

This mathematical lemma calls t=x⁰/c physical time and c a speed although c is only a positive real parameter here. State the coordinate reparametrization and rate mathematically; carry the physical reading through an appropriate physical item.

Mᵣ is defined only for r≥0, but H_f(x,s)=sM_cs f is asserted for all real s, and the Duhamel integral uses negative s when t<t₀. The assigned consumer pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations relies on this in L2 and proof 4.1, clause (e). Supply the signed-radius extension and its smoothness/evenness locally, or correct the supplier.

Proof 4.1 applies step 3.1 to h′, but that step obtains G^(1)(h)=0 from an exact vacuum family, which is not shown for h′. Derive G^(1)(h′)=0 directly from gauge invariance, then apply the harmonic-gauge identity.

Clause (e) defines S through G^(1)+Λh=S, but D subtracts κS without a λ-scaled source family; this is inconsistent with the field-law linearization and dimensionally mismatched. Define the exact stress family/residual and identify its first-order source consistently. Also δ₀ is not fixed by the supplier, so the quadratic-regime predicate is ambiguous, and the datum is local on Ω/K while the detector curves are defined on all of R.

For finite δ, g at one endpoint evaluated on the coordinate displacement is a tangent-vector norm, not the proper distance between the two bodies. Either state an infinitesimal-separation model or supply and justify the finite spatial-distance definition and its response.

J=∂rγ|₀ is an infinitesimal deviation field, but the proof identifies its acceleration with that of the finite pair γ₀ and γδ. Qualify this as a differential limit or prove a finite-separation result. Also specify the small-λ range and chart norm for ρ, and justify the O(λ²) expansion of ∂₀Γ rather than inferring it from the bound on Γ alone.
The statement begins clause 3 at u=0 but gives the cross-arm strain as a function of general u; at u=0 that strain is zero. Separate the general strain function from its value at u=0.
The final remark uses the screen-rotation law from lem-gr-tt-screen-projector, which is absent from this example’s dependencies. Add the direct prerequisite or remove the claim.

It says the quadratic residual bound is derived from the adopted field law for a family of solutions; the residual bound instead follows from the mathematical Taylor estimate once G^(1)(h)=0. It also calls curvature observable content without defining an operational observable; use gauge-invariant curvature content.

Clause (d) calls J−g(J,γ′)γ′ the normal component when g(γ′,γ′)=−1; its contraction with γ′ is 2g(J,γ′), not zero. The assigned response uses clauses (a) and (b), so this defect is not load-bearing there.

The statement says each physical worldline is the maximal geodesic, but the proof establishes only uniqueness on the common domain and the free-fall postulate does not require maximal worldlines. The assigned response uses common-domain uniqueness, not maximality.
